clue.text: Outcome of trip for Gunners? It could cause postponement of match

definitions.meaning: a stumble ends in a fall, and the Gunners are the Royal Artillery, RA, so a tumble for them is RA in a fall

definitions.text: It could cause postponement of match
definitions.meaning: a downpour can make a pitch unplayable so the game is called off

explanation.surface: A football fan wonders how Arsenal's away trip went, then thinks of the weather that might call the game off.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is cryptic: the Royal Artillery (RA, the Gunners) taking a tumble gives RA IN FALL. 'Gunners' is also Arsenal's nickname, the red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy showers waterlog a ground, a common reason for a fixture being put off.

clue.text: Selection of scattered items put together

indicators.note: Selection of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone gathers up a few odds and ends that were lying about.
explanation.definitionFit: To prepare a text or film is to assemble and arrange material, as an editor puts a book together.

clue.text: Last order from hero often misrepresented on course

indicators.note: something misrepresented is twisted out of its true shape, so the words hero often are rearranged

parts.note: a course is a route or way, a road

explanation.surface: A legend's famous final command is often garbled on the golf or race course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misrepresented' rearranges HERO OFTEN into ONE FOR THE; 'on' simply places that before ROAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A final drink bought just before leaving a pub is the parting order of the evening.

clue.text: One way to secure former standing within group

indicators.note: within says one piece sits inside the word for group

parts.note: a pack is a group, as of wolves or cards

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing means upright, so the word for former reads from the bottom up

parts.note: old means former, as in an old flame

explanation.surface: A description of how someone once held a position inside an organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: A detachable lock with a hinged shackle is a common means of fastening a gate or locker.

clue.text: Underhand elements of golf and soccer

parts.note: a round of golf is made up of eighteen holes, so one is an element of it
a corner kick is a set piece in football

explanation.surface: Someone muses on the shady sides of two sports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is taken as written between the two sporting terms.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes secret, furtive dealings, the sort conducted out of sight.

clue.text: Ribaldry exchanged between opponents? They are certainly up for it

definitions.text: They are certainly up for it

indicators.note: between says the rearranged letters sit inside the pair of letters for opponents

parts.note: in bridge East and South sit on opposing sides, giving E and S

indicators.note: exchanged suggests banter traded back and forth, signalling the letters of ribaldry change places

explanation.surface: Rival players trade crude jokes, and the clue says they are keen for it.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, East and South sit on opposing sides. 'up for it' means out of bed early, not eager.
explanation.definitionFit: People who rise at dawn are out of bed sooner than everyone, as the proverb about worms says.

clue.text: Flier's to be in France, put in place

indicators.note: put in says the French verb is inserted into the abbreviation for place

parts.note: Pl is the abbreviation for place in street names
the French verb meaning to be is être

explanation.surface: Someone flying out is told they must go to France and be settled somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a seabird, and any bird is a flier in crossword terms.

clue.text: Police raids in a remote part of Italy

indicators.note: to police is to regulate or keep in order, so the letters of raids in a are reordered

explanation.surface: Officers carry out raids in an out-of-the-way corner of Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Police' looks like the subject of 'raids' but is a verb signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: This large Mediterranean island belongs to Italy and lies well off its mainland coast.

clue.text: Half-hearted Mercian, say, rejected 18 as a rule

indicators.note: half-hearted removes one of the two middle letters of the king's name

parts.note: Offa was the eighth-century king of Mercia

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the abbreviation for say reads backwards

parts.note: e.g. is short for exempli gratia, for example, which means say

explanation.surface: A lukewarm Midlander turned down the 18 offered as a rule.
explanation.walkthrough: '18' is not a cross-reference here: it is the usual age of majority. Mercia was an Anglo-Saxon kingdom in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: In most countries a person legally becomes an adult at eighteen, reaching majority.

clue.text: Heart of problem granny?

definitions.meaning: the crux or tangle at the centre of a difficulty, as in a knotty question
a granny is a kind of tied loop, a reef tied the wrong way

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the real trouble is an elderly relative.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the tangled core of a difficulty and a tied loop such as the granny.

clue.text: Prosthetic limb worn by gangster causes unnecessary panic

indicators.note: worn by is read as the gangster's name being fitted into the phrase for an artificial limb

parts.note: a prosthetic limb is an artificial one, such as a false arm
Al Capone was the Chicago gangster, so Al stands for one

explanation.surface: A mobster wearing an artificial arm sends people into a fright.
explanation.definitionFit: A warning that turns out groundless sets off fear needlessly, like a fire bell with no fire.

clue.text: Report of man kidnapping head of state

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word for a kidnapper is said out loud

parts.note: a man who grabs someone is a seizer

explanation.surface: News of a man abducting a national leader.
explanation.definitionFit: The title was taken by Roman emperors, rulers of the empire, and later echoed in Kaiser and Tsar.

clue.text: From which you could get lamp recast?

definitions.text: From which you could get lamp recast?

parts.words: From which you could get lamp recast?
parts.note: old iron can be melted and recast as a lamp, and the letters of the two answer words also rearrange into lamp recast

explanation.surface: A question about what material a recast lamp might come from.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearranging the answer's letters gives LAMP RECAST, so the clue also works as a reversed anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Discarded iron and steel is melted down and reused, so a new lamp could be cast from it.

clue.text: Prayer involving a couple of bishops — one left in a huff

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the prayer word wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: a cry is an appeal or plea, a prayer
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, so two make BB
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A prayer with two bishops leaves one of them going off sulking.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting irritably and sulkily is to behave grumpily, as someone in a huff does.

clue.text: See 5
Definition: brief romp in metropolis

indicators.note: in says the shortened romp sits inside the word for metropolis

parts.note: a metropolis is a big city

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the last letter of the word for romp goes

parts.note: a lark is a romp, a bit of fun

explanation.surface: A dictionary-style entry for a short frolic in the big city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Definition' looks like a heading but is the definition itself, in its sense of sharpness of image.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition in a photograph or screen means sharpness, the quality of being clear and distinct.

clue.text: See 3
Pat kindly heading off to catch theologian's lecture

indicators.note: to catch means to hold, so the shortened word wraps around the theologian
heading off removes the first letter of the word for pat kindly

parts.note: to caress is to stroke or pat affectionately
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: A gentle pat sends someone off to catch a theologian's talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal talk or speech to an audience is an oration, a lecture.

clue.text: Wrinkles up, vanity half gone? It's a hazard of old age

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means reading from the bottom upwards

parts.note: wrinkles are lines on the face

indicators.note: half gone means the first three of six letters of vanity are dropped

explanation.surface: Wrinkles appear and vanity fades with years, and one more risk of growing old follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LINES into SENIL; 'half gone' leaves ITY from vanity.
explanation.definitionFit: Mental decline in the elderly, dementia or dotage, is a risk that comes with advanced years.

clue.text: Court proceedings need this periodic overhaul

definitions.meaning: in tennis every point on court begins with a player's serve
a car's routine check and maintenance at set intervals

explanation.surface: Legal hearings need a regular going-over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests a law court; it is a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the delivery that starts a tennis point and a regular mechanical check-up.

clue.text: Take part, bagging large total

indicators.note: bagging means capturing, so the word for take part holds the abbreviation

parts.note: to compete is to take part in a contest
L is the clothing abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Join in and pocket a big sum.
explanation.definitionFit: Total as an adjective means utter or entire, as in a total or complete disaster.

clue.text: Drug, one chewed and swallowed after surgery

indicators.note: after says the following pieces come behind the abbreviation for surgery

parts.note: op is short for operation, surgery
I is the Roman numeral one
to have chewed and swallowed food is to have eaten it

explanation.surface: A patient takes a painkiller, then eats something after an operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A narcotic derived from the poppy, such as morphine, is a drug used to dull pain.

clue.text: Function in East after costs reduced by 40%

indicators.note: after says the shortened word goes first, ahead of the other pieces
two of the five letters of costs is forty percent, so two are dropped

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A business event held in the East of the country after budgets were cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Function' suggests a party; here it is the trigonometric sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In trigonometry this ratio of adjacent side to hypotenuse is a mathematical function.

clue.text: See 5
Heavy plant banker's loaded in the van

indicators.note: in the van means in the vanguard, at the front, so the word for loaded leads

parts.note: piled means loaded, heaped up
in crosswords a banker is a river, something with banks

explanation.surface: A banker has stuffed a big piece of machinery into the back of a van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'van' suggests a vehicle but means the front; 'banker' is a river, not a financier.
explanation.definitionFit: Plant means industrial machinery; this machine hammers posts into the ground.

clue.text: See 3
Intrepid orator's dismissed during play

indicators.note: an orator speaks, so the following word is as heard

parts.note: in cricket a batsman is bowled when the ball hits the stumps

explanation.surface: A brave speaker is sent off in the middle of a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' suggests the theatre; it is a cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: Fearless and daring people are brave, the meaning of intrepid.

clue.text: Financial security essential for cricketer

definitions.meaning: money lodged to secure an accused person's release before trial
one of the two small wooden crosspieces resting on the stumps in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricketer needs a monetary safety net.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a bond paid for release and the crosspiece knocked off the stumps.

clue.text: Artist in island sent back formal headdress

indicators.note: sent back means the whole combination reads in reverse
in says the artist goes inside the word for island

parts.note: an ait is a small river island
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter on an island returns a grand headpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts RA in AIT making ARAIT, which 'sent back' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewelled semicircular band worn by women at grand occasions is a formal head ornament.

clue.text: Boots, perhaps, in revolutionary films

parts.note: Che Guevara was the Argentine-born revolutionary
a film is a thin layer, as is a mist on glass

explanation.surface: Footwear appears in radical movies.
explanation.walkthrough: Boots is a big British high-street pharmacy chain, not footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Boots is an example of a pharmacy, so 'perhaps' marks it as one case of the class.
